claim: John the Baptist was a real figure, executed by Herod Antipas.

bible.note: Herod has John beheaded after a banquet, at the urging of Herodias.
John preaches and baptizes in the Jordan region.

outside.note: Calls John 'the Baptist', a good man who urged Jews to live justly and be baptized. Herod feared John’s influence might lead to an uprising, so he sent him in chains to the fortress of Machaerus and had him put to death. Some Jews saw Herod’s later military defeat as God’s punishment for it. Few scholars doubt this passage.

counter: The reason for the execution differs. Josephus gives a political motive (fear of unrest) while the Gospels point to John’s criticism of Herod’s marriage to Herodias. Both can be true, but the difference should be stated. Josephus does not connect John with Jesus at all.
